### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. spinal muscular atrophy, distal, autosomal recessive, 6  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.731)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:25786)

**Proposed mechanism:** Pathogenic REEP1 variant (HP:0000001) —DISRUPTS→ REEP1 (HGNC:25786); REEP1 (HGNC:25786) —DISRUPTS→ ER-associated degradation (ERAD) pathway (GO:0030433); ER-associated degradation (ERAD) pathway (GO:0030433) —LEADS_TO→ Motor neuron dysfunction (HP:0002437); ER-associated degradation (ERAD) pathway (GO:0030433) —LEADS_TO→ Muscle weakness (HP:0001324). Loss-of-function variants in REEP1 disrupt the ER-associated degradation (ERAD) pathway, leading to motor neuron dysfunction and muscle weakness, common to both diseases.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of distinct functional consequences of REEP1 variants in each disease (e.g., one requiring gain-of-function and the other loss-of-function) would falsify this shared mechanism. Alternatively, discovery of a completely unrelated causal gene for one of the diseases would also falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: Presence of pathogenic variants in REEP1 with a minor allele frequency > 0.01 in gnomAD.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of REEP1 in the ERAD pathway could lead to therapeutic strategies targeting this pathway for both MONDO:0012453 and distal spinal muscular atrophy type 6.

Pathogenic variants in REEP1 disrupt its function in maintaining endoplasmic reticulum membrane dynamics, leading to overlapping phenotypes of spastic paraplegia and distal hereditary motor neuropathy.
